version.changelog: v1.2: explicit NO-STOP rule — never pause to ask mid-task unless truly stuck after 2 attempts

llm.summary: This autonomous task skill is broadly scoped and requires Telegram progress messages without clear opt-in or data controls.

dimensions.detail: The task-loop purpose is coherent, but the artifact also authorizes broad autonomous work such as running commands, creating files, fetching data, and writing content while sending task status externally.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Activation includes inferred autonomous tasks, not only explicit invocation, and the protocol repeatedly tells the agent not to ask or wait except after narrow failure conditions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single SKILL.md file with no executable scripts, dependencies, or suspicious installer behavior; static scan reported clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Mandatory Telegram updates are not proportionate for a general local task-execution workflow unless the user has explicitly opted in and understands what task details may leave the environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes the user's request and progress to /workspace/memory/ralph-loop.md and then deletes that file on completion, reducing auditability and user control over retention.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only for non-sensitive tasks where you are comfortable with autonomous execution, local storage of the task plan, Telegram progress updates, and deletion of the progress file afterward. Avoid it for private, regulated, credential-related, or high-impact work unless Telegram is optional, activation is explicit, and file retention is user-controlled.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: The Telegram messaging requirement is real in the artifact and is not necessary for the core local task-loop purpose; it can disclose task names, progress, errors, and file paths externally.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad activation rule based on inferred user expectations is under-scoped and can trigger autonomous behavior without explicit use of the skill.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The start-of-loop Telegram message is artifact-backed and lacks a consent gate or clear data-minimization boundary.
[SQP-2] expected: Deleting the named loop file is disclosed as part of the workflow, but automatic deletion can remove useful execution history without confirmation.
